data.narrative:
Antora Energy is a Series B climate and energy company founded by Justin Briggs, Andrew Ponec, and David Bierman, having raised $150M to date. The valuation assessment draws on a universe of one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers in the same sector, including KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, Amogy, Helion, and Redwood Materials.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression, using the $150M total raised as a proxy for post-money value and applying a typical 1.9x Series B step-up multiplier, implies a valuation of $285M. Peer-median methodology examined three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: KoBold Metals at $3.0B (Series C), Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B (Series C), and Amogy at $700M (Series C). The median across these three yields $1.0B, with a range of $700M to $3.0B.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $242M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median point of $642M. The wide dispersion between methods reflects stage and business-model variation within the climate tech peer set. Stage-progression yields a more conservative estimate tied to capital deployed, while peer-median is anchored to later-stage funding outcomes. Key uncertainties include the degree to which Antora's technology risk and path to commercialization align with Series C-stage peers versus earlier-stage valuation frameworks.
